D1_bc_lam0_pool.what: BC, lambda_prior=0 (warm-start-only), K=10 R=1 sigma_max=0.25, 4-seed pool

comparison.verdict: BC and demo_1nn lam=0 pools have overlapping 95 % CIs (BC pool centre 15.0 % vs 1-NN pool centre 11.7 %; CIs overlap by ~5 pp). The 'BC and 1-NN warm-starts are indistinguishable at lam=0' claim is substantiated, with BC running ~3 pp higher on average.

D2_1nn_lamsweep_seed0.what: demo_1nn at K=10 R=1 sigma_max=0.25, lambda sweep at seed=0
D2_1nn_lamsweep_seed0.verdict: Sharp peak at lambda=1 (75.0 %) followed by a broad plateau at 63-65 % for lambda in [2, 20]. The previous canonical lambda=5 (from exp 07's BC sweep) was sub-optimal for demo_1nn; the per-step pull benefits from a *weaker* score-bridge when the target is in-distribution. Single seed -- warrants a 4-seed pool follow-up to put a CI on the 75.0 %.

D3_1nn_sigma_tail_seed0.what: demo_1nn at K=10 R=1 lambda=5, sigma_max tail extension at seed=0
D3_1nn_sigma_tail_seed0.verdict: No cliff found. Full sigma sweep over [0.05, 1.00] (a 20x range) stays in [63.3 %, 68.3 %]. The success rate even drifts very slightly *upward* with sigma -- the bridge appears to benefit marginally from more aggressive noise when the target is in-distribution. The sigma-invariance claim is now substantiated across the full tested range, and the BC contrast becomes even sharper: BC drops from 40 % at sigma=0.03 to 0 % at sigma=0.40; 1-NN holds at ~66 % out to sigma=1.00.
